_doc: Sandown, Lake and the holiday camp: Sunnyside Holiday Camp on the edge of the village of Lake, the chalet rows, the drained pool, the outdoor stage and the play area, the boundary fence onto the Levels along the north edge with the kids' gap at the north exit, and the village road east to the seafront with a scrap of beach in the south-east corner. Positions are in 32px tiles.
name: Lake and the holiday camp

facades.name: Chalet 1
facades.locked: A card in the window: ASLEEP. DO NOT KNOCK. SERIOUSLY. The card is laminated.

facades.name: Chalet 2
facades.locked: Locked. Somebody inside is playing 'Doop' on a cassette player for what Teddy says is the fourth time.

facades.name: Chalet 4
facades.locked: Locked, and a NO VACANCIES card in the window, which on a chalet is a boast.

facades.name: Chalet 7
facades.locked: Locked. The curtains are 1970s orange and they are drawn, and have been since the 1970s.

facades.name: Chalet 8
facades.locked: Locked. Through the glass: a Teasmade, an ironing board and nobody.

facades.name: Chalet 10
facades.locked: Locked. A row of shoes on the step, smallest to largest, drying out with sand in every one.

props.name: Boundary fence
look: Chain-link, sagging. SUNNYSIDE HOLIDAY CAMP. PRIVATE. The gap beside it has been a gap for longer than the sign has been a sign.
Kids' path. Worn to the dirt. Twenty years of kids.
Two of them in particular, dear.

props.name: Boundary fence
look: The fence goes on toward the sea with a tide of crisp packets along the bottom of it.
Crisps. They call them crisps. The bag says the same thing it says at home and you still can't eat them with a straight face.

props.name: Ballroom bins
look: Two bins and a stack of crates. The smell is lager, bleach and a very old carpet.
Something's been sick in the hedge.

props.name: Beer crates
props.look: Empty crates. WHITBREAD, and under that, a sticker from the 1970s that says the same thing with less confidence.

props.name: The caretaker's mower
look: A ride-on mower, hand-painted the camp yellow. The seat is a car seat. Someone loves this.
Len. The spanners are laid out by size.

props.name: Deckchair stack
props.look: Forty deckchairs, folded, roped and padlocked. Someone counted them. Someone has been burned before.

props.name: The outdoor stage
look: An outdoor stage. Boards, a fringe of bunting, two floods on a bar. A board at the side: TALENT NIGHT 7PM. KIDS CLUB 10AM. A third line has been painted over.
Painted over, and the paint is older than the sign.
Someone very tall stood right at the front of this. I can see where the boards remember him.

props.name: Bench
look: A bench facing the stage with a bronze plate: FOR BETTY, WHO WON THE GLAMOROUS GRANDMOTHER 1978 TO 1981.
Four years running. Good for Betty.

props.name: Swings
look: A swing frame, three swings, two seats. The third chain ends in a knot and a lot of trust.
Kids don't care. Kids have never cared.

props.name: Slide
props.look: A steel slide, hot enough to brand a child. It has done so, going by the shoes beside it.

props.name: Picnic table
look: A picnic table with initials cut into every inch of it. The oldest you can find is 1962.
There's a C.R. and an F.M. about a hand apart. 1973.
There are a thousand initials, June.

props.name: Gull
props.look: A herring gull on the stage, in the exact centre, looking at you like you are late.

props.name: Camp sign
look: SUNNYSIDE HOLIDAY CAMP. EST. 1951. FAMILIES WELCOME. A sun with a face. The sun's face has been repainted, and the painter was not told what the old one looked like.
It looks like it knows something.
It looks like it is being paid to.

props.name: The old sign
look: A second sign, behind the first, faded to the bone: SUNNYSIDE. 1973 SEASON. SUNNY JIM AND THE YELLOWCOATS. CABARET NIGHTLY. KIDS' WALKABOUT DAILY.
Somebody kept that up for twenty years, dear. Somebody wanted it read.

props.name: Telephone box
look: A red phone box with every pane intact, which Teddy says is a first. It takes ten pence pieces the size of a saucer.
It rings. Sometimes. Len says don't answer it.

props.name: Vacancies sign
props.look: VACANCIES. The NO has been slid in and out so many times it hangs loose. It is out. It is the bank holiday.

props.name: Pillar box
look: A pillar box. Last collection 5.30 PM. GR, not ER: older than the Queen.
They put the king's initials on the mail boxes. I love it here.

props.name: Bench
props.look: A bench facing the ballroom doors. The wood says J.R. 1973 in a careful hand, and then a heart, and then nothing.

props.name: Coach
look: A coach on the drive. SOUTHERN VECTIS, and a card in the windscreen: BRISTOL ROVERS SUPPORTERS CLUB, SPRING TOUR.

props.name: Bicycle
props.look: A bicycle with a basket and a sign on the basket: KERRY'S. TOUCH IT AND DIE. XX.

props.name: Props crate
look: A crate with PROPS on it, and inside, a rubber chicken and a wooden sword marked TERRY'S.
Everybody's got a wooden sword marked TERRY'S.

props.name: The pool
look: The pool, drained for the season. Leaves in the deep end, a traffic cone in the shallow end, a tidemark at four feet where the fun used to stop.
Yes. That's what I'm telling myself.

props.name: Deckchair
props.look: A deckchair facing an empty pool. Optimism, or a man who has stopped asking.

props.name: Deckchair
props.look: Somebody's own deckchair, carried from home. It has a name on it in marker, like a child's coat.

props.name: Bucket and spade
look: A bucket and spade from Woolworths. The bucket is shaped like a castle and the sand inside is shaped like a bucket.
The British go to the beach to build smaller Britains.

props.name: Windbreak
props.look: A striped windbreak, folded, for a beach that is three minutes away and always in the wind.

props.name: Deckchair
props.look: A deckchair with a newspaper over the face of nobody. The newspaper is this morning's. The nobody got up.

props.name: Stile onto the beach
look: A stile over a fence that stopped existing. You could walk round it. Everybody uses the stile.
Of course they do, dear. It's there.

props.name: Yellow beach hut
look: A yellow beach hut with the number painted out. Inside, through the gap: a primus, a kettle, and a lifetime of Woman's Own.
I don't know yet. Of something.

props.name: Ice cream cart
look: WALL'S. A 99 is a cone with a chocolate stick in it and it costs 60p, which is not 99 of anything.
I've asked three people. Nobody knows why it's called that. Nobody has ever wondered.

props.name: Deckchair
look: A deckchair, unoccupied, with a towel on it, which on a British beach is a legal document.
I'm going to sit in it.

props.name: Windbreak
props.look: A windbreak, hammered in with a shoe. The shoe is still there.

props.name: Buoy
props.look: A buoy, dragged up the beach and left. NO BATHING BEYOND, it says, pointing at the chalets.

props.name: Dinghy
look: An inflatable dinghy, half down, called SANDOWN STAR in biro. Someone has been to sea in this.
Someone has been to France in this. Look at the bottom.

props.name: Gull
look: A gull with a whole chip, running from six other gulls.
Chip. Not fry. Chip. The fat here smells like a different century.

props.name: Telephone box
look: Another phone box. The directory is chained in. Somebody has written a number inside the cover and SUNNY in capitals, in pencil, faded almost to the paper.
That's a Sandown number. Old exchange. Four digits.

props.name: Parked car
look: A Vauxhall Cavalier with the steering wheel on the wrong side, parked on the wrong side, facing the wrong way.
It's the right side. We're the ones who are wrong here.

props.name: Bus stop
props.look: A bench and a pole: SOUTHERN VECTIS. The timetable says hourly and the people waiting say otherwise.

props.name: Stage curtains
look: A little stage with red curtains and a glitter backdrop that says SUNNYSIDE in a font from 1971. The boards are sprung. The springs have given up.
The air changes two steps in from the curtain. Everyone who ever stood there is still a bit there.

props.name: Staff photographs
look: Staff photos, one a season, 1971 to 1994, in a row along the wall. Yellow blazers, every year. There's a gap: a clean rectangle on the wallpaper where 1973 should be.
One missing photo in twenty-four. They took it down. They didn't move the others up.

props.name: Programme
props.look: THIS WEEK AT SUNNYSIDE. Bingo, talent night, glamorous grandmother, knobbly knees, and on Wednesday a hypnotist called The Great Marvo, with a drawing of Marvo that is not great.

props.name: Bingo
props.look: BINGO NIGHTLY. EYES DOWN 8. The 8 has been changed from a 7 with a felt pen and nobody has been told.

props.name: Calendar
props.look: Sunnyside 1994. The bank holiday is circled. Every Tuesday says COACHES. Every Saturday says CHANGEOVER in a hand that hates Saturdays.

props.name: Bar
look: A bar: Whitbread on the pump, Babycham on the shelf, a jar of pickled eggs that Teddy is not allowed to open.
They sell beer by the pint and the pint is bigger. I measured. It's bigger.

props.name: Jukebox
look: Three plays for 50p. The top slot is MR BLOBBY and the label is worn white.
I insist on knowing who Mr Blobby is.

props.name: Colour wheel
look: A colour wheel on a stand, pointed at the dance floor: red, blue, green, yellow, round and round. It would make a man all colours.
It would make a man a disco.
RYDE ELECTRICAL, 1989, on the sticker. Not the one. There might have been one.

props.name: Clock
props.look: A clock that says BULOVA and twenty past four. It is not twenty past four. It has not been twenty past four since the heatwave of '76, Len says.

props.name: Television
look: A big television on a bracket. NEIGHBOURS. The sound is off and the picture is orange.
It's Australian. They're watching Australia in England, on an island, in a holiday camp.

props.name: Fruit machine
props.look: A fruit machine, BAR-X, with a hand-lettered card: NUDGES HELD TILL TUESDAY. Somebody is coming back for them.

props.name: Lost property
look: A lost property box. Forty-three single flip-flops, a wig, a denture, and a child's cardigan with a name tape: C. RUDD.
...Twenty-one years in a box, dear. Nobody came for it.
Or it's a common name. ...It isn't.

props.name: Mirror
look: A dressing mirror with a ring of bulbs. Half of them work. The working half spells nothing, which Teddy finds a relief.

props.name: Dressing table
look: A dressing table: hairgrips, a 1992 tide table, a Sunnyside biro, a jar of cold cream. In the back of the drawer, stuck under the paper lining, a brass key on a Sunnyside fob. The fob says OFFICE in Dymo tape.
Under the lining. Somebody didn't want it found and didn't want it gone.

props.name: Yellowcoat rota, 1994
look: YELLOWCOATS, MAY 1994. Kerry. Gaz. A third name crossed out so hard the biro went through the paper, and under it, in a different hand: GONE TO BUTLINS.
They do that here. They just leave. Mid-season.

props.name: This week's rail
props.look: Three yellow blazers, a gorilla, and the back half of a pantomime horse. The front half is a matter between Gaz and Kerry.

props.name: Page-a-day calendar
props.look: A page-a-day with a joke on every page. Today's: 'What do you call a man with a seagull on his head? Cliff.' Kerry has written NO under it.

props.name: Sofa
look: A sofa that has been slept on more than sat on. There's a blanket, a hot water bottle and a copy of The Stage folded to SITUATIONS VACANT.
She's looking for a way out, poor love. They all are, in this room. Always were.

props.name: Internal phone
props.look: An internal phone. 1 for OFFICE. 2 for BAR. 3 has a strip of tape over it and nobody will say what 3 was.

props.name: Kettle
look: A kettle, a jar of Mellow Birds and a tin of custard creams with two left.

props.name: Box of balloons
props.look: Five hundred balloons and a pump. On the box, in marker: DO NOT GIVE GAZ THE PUMP.

props.name: The one working light
props.look: One bulb, bare, on a stand. Everything in here leans toward it.

props.name: Rail: the eighties
props.look: Shell suits, a Rubik's cube costume, a yellow blazer with shoulder pads you could land a plane on.

props.name: Rail: the seventies
look: The old rail. Yellow blazers from when the yellow was a different yellow. A gorilla with no head. A Dalek made of a bin.
And between the blazer and the gorilla. There.

props.name: Make-up cabinet
look: Leichner sticks, numbered. Fives and Nines for faces, barely touched. Then the colours: a full set, red, blue, green, hardly used, and the yellow worn to a stub.
Somebody painted one thing yellow, a lot, for a long time.
Or painted himself every colour there is, once.

props.name: Wig shelf
props.look: Wigs on polystyrene heads. The heads have faces drawn on. The faces have names. One of the names is TERRY.

props.name: Props crate
look: A custard pie tin, a rubber chicken, a bunch of plastic flowers that goes up a sleeve, and a tin trumpet with a note tied on: DO NOT. LEN.
A trumpet. A voice with no breath in it.

clues.name: A yellow pointed hat
clues.text: On the far rail, between a 1970s yellow blazer and a gorilla with no head: a pointed hat, yellow, as tall as your arm is long, the felt gone grey along the folds. It is not a costumier's hat. Someone built it on a wire frame and it has been worn: there's a rim of something greasy inside the band, and a thumbprint in it. Miriam already has the camera out. Teddy already has the notebook out.

clues.name: A box of receipts
clues.text: A shoebox marked HIRE, full of costume hire receipts: Gieves Theatrical, Portsmouth. One conical hat, yellow felt, and sundries, every summer since 1968. The hat has been hired every year. Which means the hat on the rail might be anybody's, and any year's.

props.name: Punch clock
props.look: A punch clock. Terry's card is in. Terry's card has been in since Thursday, and Len's has never been out.

props.name: Calendar
props.look: A calendar from Hursts of Sandown, the ironmonger. May 1994. Every day has a number of chalets let, in pencil, and the bank holiday has 48 and an exclamation mark.

props.name: Key board
look: Chalet keys, 1 to 48, on hooks. Hook 3 and hook 9 are empty. Hook 23 has two keys and a note: DO NOT LET.
Twenty-three is fine. It's just sad. Somebody died on holiday and the camp never forgave the chalet.

props.name: Notice
props.look: STAFF: NO WALKABOUTS WITHOUT THE MANAGER. Signed T.G. The paper is yellow and the drawing pins are rusted into the wall.

props.name: Filing cabinet: 1971 to 1980
look: A grey cabinet, one drawer a year. 1973 is the thin one, and the only one with a lock, and the lock is open.
Someone opens it. Someone keeps opening it.

props.name: Filing cabinet: 1981 to date
props.look: Fatter years. 1994 is already the fattest. Terry says it's the paperwork; Len says it's the complaints.

props.name: Len's desk
props.look: A desk with a blotter, a ledger, a Sunnyside biro and a mug that says WORLD'S OKAYEST GRANDAD, which Len bought himself.

props.name: Ledgers
look: Season ledgers, 1951 to date, by colour of spine. 1973 is red. The rest are green.
They ran out of green in 1973. ...Or something.

props.name: Noticeboard
look: Lost property notices. LOST: ONE CHILD, 11. FOUND: ONE CHILD, 11. SAME CHILD. And a photo of a dog that found its own way home from Shanklin.
That's good. That's a good dog.

props.name: Photocopier
props.look: A photocopier with a sign: OUT OF ORDER SINCE THE WAR. Len's handwriting. Len is sixty-one.

props.name: Lost and found cabinet
props.look: A cabinet of things people left in 1994 and will not come back for: a cagoule, a Walkman, a cassette of 'Now 27' with the case of 'Now 26'.

clues.name: The 1973 staff rota
clues.text: In the thin drawer, on top of everything: the 1973 staff rota, typed, with a coffee ring. SUNNY JIM (ENTERTAINMENTS) is on every day of May, and then a line through the 29th and onward, and in the margin, in a young man's hand: LEFT 29/5. NO FWD ADDRESS. NOT TO BE REHIRED. T.G. The spring bank holiday was the 28th.

props.name: The big bed
props.look: A double bed with a candlewick bedspread and a hot water bottle, in May.

props.name: The small bed
props.look: A single bed with a Thunderbirds duvet and a comic under the pillow. The comic has been read in the dark.

props.name: Welcome card
props.look: YOUR HOLIDAY STARTS HERE! A sun with a face, in a font nobody has updated since 1971. The exclamation mark is doing a lot of work.

props.name: Television
look: A portable telly on a chain. Four channels, and the fourth is a snowstorm with a voice in it.

props.name: Drawer
look: A Gideon Bible, a 1994 Island Line timetable and sixteen pence in brown coins the size of medals.
That's two pence. It's worth two pence, Teddy.
It's the size of a cookie.

props.name: Beach bag
props.look: A beach bag: a towel, factor 4, a Mills and Boon, and a bag of chips from last night, cold, which Sandra will eat.

props.name: Bucket
props.look: A bucket with a crab in it. The crab has a name and a grievance.

props.name: Kettle
props.look: A kettle, two mugs, a half-pint of milk on the windowsill. The windowsill is the fridge.

props.name: Gaz's bed
props.look: An unmade bed, a yellow blazer on the floor, a can of Red Stripe on the sill. Gaz is not a morning person. Gaz is not, strictly, an afternoon person.

props.name: Kerry's bed
props.look: Made. Hospital corners. A copy of The Stage and a letter to Butlins, Minehead, stamped and not posted.

props.name: Wardrobe rail
props.look: Two yellow blazers and a dinner jacket that Gaz calls his 'Vegas'. There is no Vegas.

props.name: Training poster
look: YELLOWCOAT RULES: SMILE. SING. NEVER SAY NO. NEVER BE SEEN WITHOUT THE BLAZER. The fifth rule has been cut off with scissors.
Cut. Not torn. Somebody did that carefully.

props.name: Box under the bed
look: A box that came with the chalet, Kerry says; they just push it back under. Inside: greasepaint sticks fused into one rainbow lump, a lampshade frame bent into a cone, a mouth-organ, and a 1973 Sunnyside name badge. SUNNY JIM.
He was tall. Not as tall as the hat. The hat did the rest, and he knew it.
That's a frame for a hat. That's the frame for the hat.
He sat on this bed and built it, dear. And then he went and did it to two children, and then he ran.

props.name: Television
props.look: A telly with a coat hanger for an aerial. It gets Radio 1 better than it gets pictures.
